title: GitHub Release notes are read from the operator's working-tree CHANGELOG, not the tagged commit (pair with quest-cli)
description: Found by the LCLI-622 reviewer (opum-workflow:reviewer, branch feat/LCLI-622-executed-github-release at 30571a09, 2026-09-28). This is a design point shared with quest, not a regression. scripts/github-release.mjs releaseNotesFor reads join(root, 'CHANGELOG.md') from the checkout promote-latest.mjs runs in. So an uncommitted edit, or an edit landed after the tag, becomes the body of a NEW vX release, and nothing checks the notes against the tagged commit. An EXISTING release is safe: differing notes are refused and never edited. Sections do get edited after release. The reviewer's live comparison: v0.11.0, 0.9.3, 0.9.2, 0.9.1, 0.8.0, 0.7.0, 0.6.2 and 0.6.0 match their current CHANGELOG sections, while v0.9.0 and v0.6.1 do not. The LCLI-622 pairing recorded this as MATCH with quest-cli QCLI-398 (both read the working tree), so changing it is a paired change. Suggested rule: read CHANGELOG.md from the commit v<X> peels to (git show <peeled>:CHANGELOG.md, a commit promote-latest.mjs already resolves in step 1), for both the pre-move refusal and the cut. Also noted, theoretical: a '## ' line inside a fenced code block would silently truncate a section, in both repos' extractors.

A test proves a working-tree CHANGELOG edit that is not in the tagged commit does not reach the release body
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

Implement in scripts/github-release.mjs: a pinned gh-api reader for CHANGELOG.md at a commit (precedent: check-breaking-bump.mjs:186), releaseNotesFor taking the text rather than a path, and the standalone repair main() resolving the tag first so the repair tool cuts the same bytes the preflight compares

IMPLEMENTED at c6c248b1 (branch fix/LCLI-639-release-notes-from-tagged-commit, pushed; no PR yet). The rule agreed with quest-cli as QCLI-407 is implemented as agreed: notes and title come from CHANGELOG.md's bytes AT the commit v<version> peels to, for the pre-move refusal, the cut and the repair tool alike; no deviation.

WHAT CHANGED. scripts/github-release.mjs: new exported changelogAtRefArgs(sha) and readChangelogAtCommit(sha, {execFile}) -- one pinned `gh api --hostname github.com -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/contents/CHANGELOG.md?ref=<sha>` read (check-breaking-bump.mjs's quest-side shape), returning {changelog, source, error}, never throwing, 8 MiB buffer, and refusing a value that is not a 40-hex commit sha so the read cannot silently become a moving ref. releaseNotesFor(version, {changelog}) is now a pure function of the TEXT: the changelogPath seam is gone from the module, its main(), promote-latest.mjs and both .d.mts. main() (repair/backfill) resolves the tag FIRST via pair-receipt's resolveTagCommit, so a tag that does not resolve refuses at exit 1 before any gh call that writes; exit codes stay 0/1/2. scripts/promote-latest.mjs: changelogPath deleted; step 9 reads CHANGELOG.md at peeled.commit (resolved in step 1) and step 13 reuses that capture, sound because the commit is immutable. Both refusals reworded: the tag is immutable, so a missing or empty section at that commit cannot be fixed in this checkout -- the honest remedies are re-tagging v<version> or cutting the release by hand with notes you choose. changelogSection gained the QCLI-407 fence parity (open /^ {0,3}(```|~~~)/, close with nothing after but space/tab; a bare "```" opens rather than closing on itself; an unclosed fence runs to EOF with the trailing link-reference trim intact) and still normalises CRLF before the split. scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs deliberately untouched: it reads the working tree because it gates the bump before any tag exists. docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md item 9, the repair-command paragraph and post-latest item 2 now state the tagged-commit rule and the honest remedy; CHANGELOG.md has one [Unreleased] ### Fixed bullet.

EVIDENCE. test/lcli639-release-notes-from-tagged-commit.test.ts: a tmpdir checkout whose CHANGELOG.md carries an edit no tag carried, driven through the promote path (--dry-run and --promote, both reaching the cut) and the repair tool; both cut the COMMITTED bytes, and the contents read is asserted at the peeled sha. Controls: the vendored pre-change module (test/fixtures/lcli639/github-release.pre-change.mjs = `git show fee53bc6:scripts/github-release.mjs`, blob 6dde69ea, re-derived by the suite from the bytes below its header) and promote-latest.mjs mutated back to the defect's shape BOTH cut the working-tree edit, so the fixture is proven to discriminate rather than assumed to. Fence vectors (i)-(iv) plus a fenced-CRLF case live in test/github-release.test.ts. Live read-only measurements on the real repository (node scripts/github-release.mjs --version <v>, never --create): 0.11.0 exit 0, "release v0.11.0 exists; would mark it latest"; 0.9.0 exit 0 now, "would mark it latest" -- run against the PRE-CHANGE module with this checkout's CHANGELOG.md it reported "its notes differ from the CHANGELOG section", which is this defect on production data; 0.6.1 exit 1 under BOTH readings, so that mismatch is not the working-tree drift LCLI-639 names (the section at its tag differs from the shipped body -- a separate fact, and the tool correctly refuses to edit an existing release); 0.10.0 exit 1, "refs/tags/v0.10.0 could not be read" (there is no such tag; the refusal now precedes any notes read).

DEVIATION FROM THE HANDOFF BRIEF, deliberate and reasoned: the control could not be `git show 0305ca90^:scripts/github-release.mjs` resolved at test time. This repository's CI checks out at depth 1 (ci.yml's actions/checkout steps carry no fetch-depth; only main-fast-forward-guard.yml sets 0), so that control would FAIL in CI, not merely go stale -- a green local run would be bought with a red gate. The pre-change module is vendored into test/fixtures/lcli639/ instead (documented in test/fixtures/README.md, precedent: test/fixtures/quest-cli/version-parity.mjs), with its git blob id re-derived by the suite; the promote path's control is the current module mutated back to the defect's shape, anchored on the fixed line so the mutation is a no-op -- and the control therefore fails loudly -- if a later edit moves it. Second, smaller deviation: the dry run's detail reports only the BYTE LENGTH of the notes, never their text, so the dry-run assertion is on that length, chosen so the two candidate sources' lengths differ (asserted in the fixture's own describe).

DELTA IMPLEMENTED at ac2ee5a9 (branch fix/LCLI-639-release-notes-from-tagged-commit, pushed). The fence predicate is now the refined rule both reviews found and quest-cli already implements -- implemented identically on both sides, not renegotiated.

WHY. Three defects, each reproduced first-party against the committed extractor: (1) a tilde line inside a backtick fence closed it and truncated the section (body "```md
alpha
~~~" for a document whose fence ran to the closing ```) -- the incomplete fix, not a regression; (2) a four-marker fence never closed, so the section swallowed the next entry (body "````
alpha
````

older") -- a regression the fence rule itself introduced; (3) a fenced "## [X]" line was taken as START and the section then ran to EOF -- also a regression, where the pre-change body was wrong but bounded ("```").

WHAT CHANGED. scripts/github-release.mjs: the section-local boolean toggle is replaced by fenceState(lines), a whole-document scan that remembers the opener's CHARACTER and RUN LENGTH and records every line's state; a closer must repeat the opener's character at least as many times, with nothing but whitespace after it, and a BACKTICK fence's info string may not itself contain a backtick ("```a`b" opens nothing). changelogSection takes START as the first heading line outside a fence and END as the first unfenced `## ` line after it; no unfenced section at all is null, so a fenced `## [X]` cannot hijack one. An unclosed fence still runs to EOF, keeping the trailing link-reference trim. The two-regex toggle is replaced, not kept alongside. The docblock states the SCOPE as a decision rather than an omission: the fence state is implemented and nothing else of CommonMark -- no indented-code-block interaction, no lazy continuation, no container or list scoping.

REVIEW NITS CLOSED at acc73e3c (branch fix/LCLI-639-release-notes-from-tagged-commit, pushed). Four of the five nits; all additive, none touching shipped behaviour, the fence rule or the vendored fixture. Each new or changed test had its prediction written first and then measured, both in this checkout and against mutations in a scratch mirror.

F1 (the e2e file proved its point with the same builder the stub answers). test/lcli639-release-notes-from-tagged-commit.test.ts now asserts the contents read's argv against CONTENTS_ARGV, a literal carrying the fixture's peeled sha: `gh api --hostname github.com -H Accept: application/vnd.github.raw repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/contents/CHANGELOG.md?ref=aaaaaaaa...`. The builder-derived form is gone from all three places it appeared (the dry-run assertion, the --promote assertion, and the repair tool's call-order slice). PREDICTION: with `changelogAtRefArgs` pointed at `?ref=main` in a scratch mirror, the OLD file stays green and the NEW file reddens exactly the three argv assertions plus the runbook pin's (b) half. MEASURED: old file (from git at ac2ee5a9) 8 pass / 0 fail -- the reviewer's own finding reproduced; new file 7 pass / 4 fail, failing at the dry-run argv (line 442), the --promote argv (line 466), the repair call-order slice (line 552) and the runbook pin's builder half (line 618).

F2 (the missing state: a FAILED contents read). world({changelogAtCommit: "fail"}) answers the raw-contents read with gh's non-zero HTTP 502. Two tests: "a FAILED contents read refuses, and never falls back to this checkout's CHANGELOG.md" (the checkout's CHANGELOG.md is asserted to hold a real, non-empty section first -- the fallback's bait -- then --dry-run and --promote must both exit 1 naming the remote source, with no release call, no notes file and no registry write), and "and with the local CHANGELOG.md unreadable, the refusal still names the remote source" (the local path is replaced by a DIRECTORY, so any read of it fails with EISDIR on every platform; the refusal must still be the remote one and must not name the local path). PREDICTION: a fallback mutant -- `if (!changelogRead.changelog) changelogRead = { source: join(root, "CHANGELOG.md"), changelog: await readFile(...) }`, i.e. exactly the regression the reviewer described -- reddens those two tests and leaves the rest green. MEASURED: 8 pass / 3 fail; the two intended tests failed, and the third red was the pre-change control's own DEFECT_ANCHOR guard firing because the mutant moved the line that guard is anchored on (a designed property of the control, not a defect). Before this nit the whole file was green under gh 502 plus an uncommitted section, which is the defect itself.

F3 (one contents read per --promote run). The --promote test now also asserts `contentsReads(w)).toEqual([CONTENTS_ARGV])`, pinning step 13's reuse of step 9's capture. PREDICTION: a mutant that re-reads at step 13 (same sha, same bytes, invisible to a deterministic stub) reddens that test alone. MEASURED: 9 pass / 2 fail -- the intended red, plus the pre-change control's stricter "no contents read at all" assertion, which also sees the extra read.

F4 (the mutation comment's arithmetic). The block at the head of the fence vectors in test/github-release.test.ts now says thirteen fence tests (the eight vectors there and the five above), seven red and six green, with the red set unchanged -- (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (g) and (f-bracketed); (f) and the five earlier vectors stay green. The harness carried twelve of the thirteen (the fenced-CRLF pair differs only in line endings) and measured 7 red / 5 green, as predicted.

F5 (the runbook's command was compared to nothing). One new test, "the runbook's command is the argv the module sends": the runbook's literal command (hand-written in the test, with a sample sha substituted for its `<that commit>` slot) must be present in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md, and `changelogAtRefArgs(<sample sha>)` must produce that same literal, modulo the shell quoting of the header, which the test removes and nothing else. PREDICTION: doc drift reddens the doc half only; builder drift reddens the builder half only. MEASURED, in the scratch mirror: builder pointed at `main` -> red at the builder half (line 618) with the doc half green; the runbook's `?ref=<that commit>` drifted to `?ref=<commit>` -> red at the doc half (line 616) with the rest of the file green (10 pass / 1 fail). The two halves are independently sensitive, which is what keeps F5 from repeating F1's weakness.
